csv_project_name: Architect For Edgerton Park - Adaptive Use Assessment
csv_agency: City of New Haven Purchasing Dept
csv_scope_of_work: The purpose of the project is to produce a report of the Edgerton Park Carriage House and Greenhouses current existing conditions and produce a report to include all items addressed in the scope of work below. The project requires a qualified Historical Architect. The proposer is expected to coordinate efforts with the project coordinator for New Haven Parks. The Consultant will: -Consult with New Haven Parks representatives and/or their designee(s) regarding the needs and goals of the project. -Produce a report that includes the following: An assessment of the resource s current, existing conditions including a summary description and evaluation of the building systems including Mechanical, electrical and plumbing, HVAC and fire protection

title: Architect for Edgerton Park - Adaptive Use Assessment
short_description: Assessment of historic park buildings for adaptive reuse and existing-condition reporting.
project_location: Edgerton Park, New Haven, Connecticut, USA
project_scope: Preparation of an adaptive use assessment report for the Edgerton Park Carriage House and Greenhouses. Scope includes documenting current existing conditions and providing a summary description and evaluation of building systems, including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and fire protection. The assignment is for a qualified historical architect and involves coordination with New Haven Parks.
services: Architectural services focused on historic preservation and adaptive reuse assessment; existing-condition survey/reporting; coordination with park representatives; multidisciplinary input listed for civil engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, land use planning, electrical, fire protection, mechanical, utility engineering, and urban studies/planning/design.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily an architectural/historic preservation assessment, not structural design.
- Focus is existing-condition reporting for park buildings, with strong MEP/building systems emphasis.
- No indication of complex load-bearing structures, long spans, bridges, roofs, or special structures.
- Small contract value suggests limited engineering scope and low strategic relevance for sbp.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction cost is stated. The document only gives a contract value of 40000 USD for consulting/report services. Useful cost-related information: adaptive reuse assessment of a carriage house and greenhouses in a historic park; no area, dimensions, or construction budget provided, so no realistic construction-cost estimate is possible.
fee_explanation: No explicit fee for structural engineering or sbp-relevant services is stated. The only stated amount is the overall consultant contract value of 40000 USD, which covers architectural assessment/reporting and multidisciplinary review.
references_qualifications: Qualified Historical Architect required. Disciplines requested include architecture, historic preservation, civil engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, land use planning, electrical engineering, fire protection engineering, mechanical engineering, utility engineering, and urban studies/planning/design.
